holidays.name: National Oatmeal Nut Waffles Day
holidays.description: Waffles get a hearty upgrade today. Toasty oats and crunchy nuts go into the batter, which turns a plain breakfast into something closer to a cozy trail-mix hug. Top them with butter, maple syrup or fruit and call it a balanced meal.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on fun-holiday calendars for breakfast lovers.
holidays.funFact: Waffle batter is cooked in a patterned iron, and those deep grid pockets are designed to hold syrup and melted butter.

holidays.name: Johnny Appleseed Day
holidays.description: A day to honor John Chapman, the barefoot, tin-pot-hatted wanderer of American folklore who spread apple trees across the frontier. Celebrate by eating something apple-y or planting a tree.
holidays.origin: John Chapman was born in Massachusetts in 1774. He spent decades planting apple nurseries across Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana and beyond. Some sources date his death to March 1845, and the day is observed in his memory.
holidays.funFact: Most of Chapman's apples were small and tart, and people mainly used them for hard cider, not for eating.

holidays.name: World Plumbing Day
holidays.description: A salute to the unsung heroes behind every working tap, toilet and shower. The day celebrates how plumbing protects public health and gets clean water to the people who need it.
holidays.origin: The World Plumbing Council launched it in 2010 to raise awareness of the importance of plumbing for health, safety and sanitation worldwide.
holidays.funFact: The word plumber comes from the Latin word for lead, plumbum, because ancient Roman pipes were often made of lead.
